text:
maria: heads-up, saw a TLS handshake spike in apac region at ~2026-03-20T12:10Z, lots of proxy->ingest failures. opening thread to correlate with the rotator RBAC change earlier today

devon: ack — do we know which service is failing the handshake? any cert errors in logs?

maria: proxy logs show `tls: handshake failure` and `alert 40`. sample: 
```
2026-03-20T12:11:05Z proxy[ingest]: tls_handshake: error: tls: handshake failure (alert 40)
2026-03-20T12:11:05Z proxy[ingest]: peer_cert: CN=svc-ingest.apac.internal, cert_chain_len=2
2026-03-20T12:11:06Z proxy[ingest]: transport: handshake completed=0
```

jess: we deployed the keystore RBAC policy at 09:00Z to scope KMS decrypt to `keystore-rotator@infra`. rolled out to apac last. could be related.

kai: I see error spikes from the cert-rotator logs too: `failed to decrypt private key: access denied`. small snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T09:02:12Z rotator[apac]: ERROR failed to decrypt /var/run/certs/svc-ingest.key: AccessDeniedException: Missing kms:Decrypt permission for key arn:aws:kms:apac:111:key/xxxx
```

maria: that lines up. when rotator can't decrypt key material, proxies still try to use on-disk certs but session ticket resumption + stapled OCSP maybe mismatched so handshake fails intermittently.

devon: any recent IAM/KMS policy principals changed? jess mentioned scoping to `keystore-rotator@infra` — did that remove any service accounts used by edge proxies?

jess: the change removed a broad role `keystore-decryptor` and added a narrower role. I thought only rotator needed it, but looks like proxy sidecar also calls KMS for session ticket keys and key unwrap.

sre-bot: alert: TLS-handshake-failure-rate apac > 5% for 5m. Incident link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0319-APAC-TLS

kai: ok plan: 1) rollback the RBAC change to restore previous decrypt permissions 2) restart rotator and proxy sidecar to pick up restored keys 3) collect audit logs (KMS, IAM) for the window 09:00-12:30Z 4) followup with tighter principal scoping after we validate which principals actually need decrypt.

maria: +1. I'm going to run a quick check to confirm which principals attempted Decrypt and were denied. running query on audit logs now.

auditor-bot: query result partial: `kms:Decrypt` denies: principals: ["proxy-sidecar@apac", "cert-rotator@apac"], resource: arn:aws:kms:apac:111:key/xxxx, timeframe: 2026-03-20T09:00Z-12:15Z. full log: https://logs.internal/apac/kms/6660001111

devon: looks conclusive. We should roll back and then do a planned scoping: allow `keystore-rotator@infra` and `proxy-sidecar@apac` the decrypt action but remove other broad principals. Also add a conditional on source VPC tag.

jess: I'm reverting policy now. will push quick rollback to org-iam and patch rotator.

maria: rolling proxies in apac after rollback. staging confirms handshake rate drops.

sre-bot: update: TLS-handshake-failure-rate apac down to 0.9% after 12:22Z.

kai: postmortem action items: - create explicit allow-list for KMS decrypt per service + region - add unit test to rotator CI to validate decrypt permission in a dry-run - improve alerting to include KMS deny rate correlated with TLS handshake spikes - document rollback playbook for RBAC changes

devon: and add an audit alert (auditor-bot) to trigger when KMS denies exceed threshold and coincide with TLS errors.

jess: opened PR #8345 to reintroduce scoped decrypt for rotator + proxies with VPC condition and least-priv principal. I'll include a rollback tag and verification steps.

maria: thanks. keeping this open until we've verified full global sweep. will update incident ticket with timeline and links. :white_check_mark:
